body:
WHAT
While OVERDRIVE is on, before each root (non-child) turn starts, the session runs `git stash create` in the workspace and keeps the returned commit ref. The ref is reported as `overdriveSnapshot` on that turn's `turn_finished` event so the user can recover tracked files an autonomous turn deleted or rewrote. Nothing is reported when the tree was clean (empty output), when the workspace is not a git repo, or when git fails.

WHY
OVERDRIVE runs deletions without asking; without a parked snapshot a wrong autonomous deletion of tracked, uncommitted work would be unrecoverable.

WHERE
engine/core/src/runtime/session.ts — Session.snapshotForOverdrive() (existsSync(.git) check, execFile('git', ['stash','create','overdrive pre-turn snapshot']), overdriveSnapshotRef), the call in Session.runTurn() guarded by `this.overdrive && !this.opts.child`, and the turn_finished emit spreading `overdriveSnapshot` only when overdrive is on and the ref is defined.

TEST CHECKLIST
1. In a git repo with a modified tracked file and setOverdrive(true), running a FakeProvider turn emits turn_finished with overdriveSnapshot matching /^[0-9a-f]{40}$/ and `git cat-file -t <ref>` reports 'commit'.
2. Same repo with a clean tree: turn_finished has no overdriveSnapshot key.
3. A cwd without a .git directory never runs git and turn_finished has no overdriveSnapshot key.
4. With OVERDRIVE off and a dirty tree, no snapshot is taken and turn_finished has no overdriveSnapshot.
5. A child session (opts.child true) does not snapshot even in OVERDRIVE; and a failing git binary does not prevent the turn from running (the turn still emits turn_finished).
